summary: A local news feature previewing the city's autumn 2023 cultural festival season, which begins September 5 and runs through October 15. It argues that festivals preserve heritage against globalization and build community, then walks through each event with its date and organizer or spokesperson. Events include a lantern festival, food bazaar, dance and music festival, craft fair, carnival, film festival, language symposium and a closing feast.
one_line: Preview of the city's autumn 2023 cultural festival calendar, from the Lunar Lantern Festival to the Unity Feast, stressing heritage preservation and inclusivity.
key_facts: The city's autumn cultural festivities kick off on September 5, 2023.
The Lunar Lantern Festival is on September 9 and features thousands of paper lanterns and a lantern releasing ceremony symbolizing letting go of past worries; organizer Mei Lin leads it.
The Global Food Bazaar runs September 15 and 16 at Riverside Promenade, organized by Alejandro Mendoza, with dishes like South Asian curries, Eastern European stews and North African tagines.
The Dance and Music Festival is on September 21 at the Cultural Arts Center and includes Flamenco, Bharatanatyam and Irish step dancers; Simone Dubois emphasizes its importance.

The Heritage Craft Fair on September 27 offers demonstrations of pottery making, weaving and woodworking and also serves as a marketplace; master weaver Josephine Clark says it is about "preserving skills that define our cultural identity".
The Cultural Carnival on October 1 is the pinnacle of the season, with a parade of traditional attire and floats; organizer Martin Diaz says it should showcase the community as one.
The Cultural Film Festival runs October 6-8 with international films, documentaries and shorts on cultural stories and legends; festival director is Raj Patel.

The Indigenous Language Symposium on October 12 aims to preserve dwindling native languages through workshops, discussions and language classes; Dr. Maria Torres says "Every language conveys an entire worldview."
The Unity Feast on October 15 closes the season, inviting people of diverse backgrounds to share a meal with equal respect.
The article argues cultural festivals preserve traditions against globalization's homogenizing effects and strengthen the community against divisiveness.
